rows.meaning: This pull request is a code-review forum, not a per-username voting forum.
Reviews are weighted by the merit of their arguments rather than their posting frequency.
A participant need not repost a point already made here or on #28130.
Leaving unsubstantiated or repeated ACKs/NACKs is discouraged on the stated ground that it only spams subscribers.
Expressing disgust is rejected as a reasonable use case for Bitcoin Core.
Deprecated is proposed to mean only that developers recommend not using the feature.
Consult the linked C gets() example in the discussion of deprecation without prompt removal.
The reported recommendation is not to set the option below the default value.
Marking the option deprecated is considered reasonable even if a few developers strongly disagree.
Whether or when to remove rather than merely deprecate the option depends on user appreciation, support effort, and perhaps harmful network effects.
Retain the option given current user demand and very low maintenance effort.
If the option is removed from Core and users actually want it, they can patch it back in.
If the option is removed from Core and users actually want it, they can use a derivative that restores it for them.
Add an assertion like the specified assert_greater_than test unless the property is already tested another way.
If the property should not be tested, it probably should not be documented either.
Consult DrahtBot issue 51 for the known bot-updating issue.
One attributed camp says to remain proactive toward spam filtration despite lacking a completely effective solution.
Only the majority decides the debate's winner; argument does not decide it.
Smaller code changes can be left to followups in this PR, with the stated review-tracking difficulty as the reason.
Bitcoin Core generally provides very limited accommodation to forks, including altcoins, modified implementations, and experimental features.
Including fork accommodations of the cited CLIENT_NAME/SKIP_BRANCH_PUSH kinds requires some convincing.
The quoted speaker expresses a slight preference for the closed proposal that removes the option completely.
At this point the speaker prefers not to switch back, because this PR has received more review and subsequent improvements.
Consult Bitcoin Core PRs 28052 and 28207 in support of the disk-obfuscation explanation.
Replace the deprecated designation for -datacarrier and -datacarriersize with wording that these options are not recommended for use.
Do not open a proposal to remove these options for a few more years.
There should not be removal warnings if there is no current plan actually to remove the options.
Consult the specific corecheck.dev page for details on this PR's coverage and benchmarks.
Consult the linked contribution guideline for information on the review process.
If a review is incorrectly listed, react to this comment with a thumbs-down.
Following the requested correction reaction, the bot will ignore it on the next update, with the pronoun's referent left open.
Do not add more arguments to the node.
The proposed conservative approach leaves the existing defaults as they are.
Allow the setting to be increased for those who choose to increase it.
Alternatively set a high default limit so a node runner can set a lower value.
Keep conceptual discussion on the specified corresponding mailing-list thread.
Lift the restriction on the number of OP_RETURN outputs per transaction to permit the described less harmful data-storage approach.
The speaker still advocates doing PR #32359.
Add the supplied two-line OP_RETURN test comment, including its Add one more byte wording.
The decision about backporting this change, including the 30-series release question, is described as a maintainer's call.
The speaker commits not to put up a fuss whichever way that release/backport decision goes.
Add -locations none to the LCONVERT invocation in translate.cmake, as suggested by the quoted question.
Prefer are not recommended to be used over have been marked as deprecated because it is clearer to users.
Discouragement is deprecation.
Revise the phrase after a deprecation warning, which the speaker evaluates as weird.
The speaker invokes open-source principles as requiring transparent decision-making that respects diverse input.
The addressed participant should keep comments on topic in this thread.
Comments about maintainers, other specific people, drama, and similar matters are not on topic in this thread.
The addressee may take those topics to bitcoin-core/meta if desired.
Failure to focus future comments on review of the proposed changes is said to result in a temporary ban for the addressed participant.
If the addressee wants to debate this moderation comment, do so on bitcoin-core/meta.
If debating this moderation comment, do not do so here.
Consult the linked moderation guidelines for more information on this policy.
The conceptual endorsement assumes a long interval before reconsidering deprecation.
There must be no translation-source updates after the final translation string freeze.
Remove deprecation of datacarrier and datacarriersize by reverting the specified commit from PR #32406.
Bitcoin Core has followed a best practice of avoiding an option when developers cannot articulate when it should be used.
Do not offer users footguns.
